name: Nia Brooks
quote: Give me space to read, and make the important idea easy to find.
bio: Nia is a graphic design student with dyslexia. She prefers larger text, clear headings, and a calm page with plenty of space between ideas.
priorities: Read comfortably, follow the discussion, and keep her own notes easy to find.
changes: A wide reading area leads the page. Notes use 20–22 px Inter with generous line spacing. Mint marks the active location; sources sit in a separate strip. A read-aloud control is pictured as a concept.
hierarchy: Personal notes → group discussion → course materials
prompt: Use a warm paper background with mint highlights. Give my notes larger text and more spacing. Keep the group conversation nearby, but let my own ideas lead the page.

name: Leo Park
quote: Let me see which ideas connect while the conversation is still happening.
bio: Leo is an interaction design student who prefers arranging ideas spatially. He uses color and position to remember how a question developed from an earlier thought.
priorities: See relationships, compare notes at once, and keep the group discussion in view.
changes: A large idea board replaces the notebook column. Labeled cards and connecting lines show relationships. A compact icon rail frees up canvas space, while a chat column preserves the conversation.
hierarchy: Idea relationships → group discussion → source connections
prompt: Put my notes on a visual board. Use blue, pink, and cyan to distinguish labeled note types, show how ideas connect, and keep the discussion visible on the right.

name: Sam Rivera
quote: Show me what to do next, then keep everything I need within reach.
bio: Sam is a digital media student who commutes and works part time. He studies in short sessions and prefers a dark interface with compact information and obvious next steps.
priorities: Prepare for the next discussion quickly and resume work without hunting through screens.
changes: Discussion preparation becomes a prominent checklist. Horizontal navigation opens more space for a dense chat and notes view. Notes become compact rows; yellow identifies priority and orange marks an action.
hierarchy: Next discussion task → chat and note list → process and materials
prompt: Give me a dark workspace with yellow priorities and orange actions. Put the next discussion task first, and show my chat, notes, sources, and progress in a compact overview.
